AUTHORED SYNTHETIC CONTROLS

Run the fixed methods on the selected authored examples.

Multilingual model experiment

Actual local inference on the 64 fictional source texts. Model assets remain on the local runner; this site loads its retained scores. No paid API call or live-source inference is performed.

What this measures

A related report describes the same underlying event, even if it repeats a source or contradicts the original allegation. Relatedness does not establish truth, independent corroboration or danger.

There are 16 authored queries and 48 candidate reports across two partitions. Each query has three candidates, including difficult negatives. Both partitions and their labels are visible to the developer: this is a diagnostic control set, not independent or blinded validation. Text and story families are checked for overlap across partitions; broader template similarity remains.

Methods, denominators and limits

Current TF-IDF: the actual workbench matcher, using its cosine threshold of 0.18 and minimum three shared tokens. Corpus weighting includes the query report, as in the workbench.

BM25 challenger: fixed k1 = 1.2, b = 0.75; candidate-only corpus statistics, unique query terms and a minimum three shared tokens. Positive scores are ranked without a tuned threshold. Its score is not on the cosine scale. This compares two complete retrieval policies, including different acceptance rules.

The lexical methods use the same bounded Unicode tokenizer. The saved encoder uses its own pretrained tokenizer, a 128-token limit and rejection of truncation. Methods use report text and known-by dates; authored labels, explanations and family names are supplied only to the evaluator after ranking. The lexical methods do not translate or extract event dates. The saved MiniLM run uses normalized mean-pooled 384-dimensional embeddings from the pinned quantized model. It ranks positive cosine scores without a three-token overlap gate or tuned threshold. It is a retrieval encoder, not an event-identity classifier. Publication and recording dates determine availability; they are not event dates.

Quoted-context ordering: unique explicit date or same-script fictional-place mismatches move candidates later in the MiniLM queue. No candidates are removed and scores are unchanged. Missing or compatible mentions do not establish an event match. The narrow parser supports English/Hindi day-month expressions, ISO dates and named fictional sites. It does not attach mentions to events, infer years or resolve aliases. Rules were developed after inspecting these authored failures; corrections can trigger misleading flags.

First-result success counts a related first result over all queries. Wrong, unresolved and empty first results remain separate. Recall@3 is the mean fraction of known related reports retrieved within the first three results. MRR averages reciprocal rank of the first related result; missing results contribute zero. Unresolved candidates are never counted as confirmed errors or confirmed matches. Future candidates are excluded from both corpus weighting and scoring.

Eight examples per partition do not establish deployment accuracy. Both partitions and labels were visible while developing these methods. No method is promoted automatically, and no workspace, forecast or alert is changed. All results are calculated locally without API charges.

Review event context

Use exact quotations from each original report. Review event place and event time separately. A similarity score does not decide whether these are the same event.

A same-event proposal requires reviewed place and event-time matches, quoted from both reports. A different-event proposal needs a quoted conflict. When context is missing, retain Insufficient context. Translations and interpretations remain reviewer judgments.
